artifacts.summary: Resolves the mandatory task-type-detection decision (narrow multi-word keyword_overrides; residual .lean-anchor gap spawned to core, not absorbed) and the mandatory reconciliation-ownership decision (recommend moving the already-scoped /reconcile work into books, not rebuilding it here) with live-measured evidence; corrects the dispatch's stale book-directory-layout and certifier-landed-state grounding against the live Verification repo; decides two routing blocks only, books:certify (not books:document) as the sole compound sub-route, --hard agent variants justified, and both /book and /certify as separate commands.

memory_candidates.content: In this agent-system's task-type detection (task-type-detect.sh), strong anchors for meta/lean4 resolve BEFORE any extension's keyword_overrides are scanned, and the keyword_overrides scan itself is alphabetical-by-extension-directory-name, first-match-wins, final (no alias remap). A new extension whose directory name sorts early (e.g. 'books' sorts before 'core') is scanned ahead of every other extension's overrides, so its keywords must be narrow/multi-word to avoid capturing other extensions' tasks; and any description naming a '.lean' file is captured by the lean4 strong anchor unconditionally, before any extension's own keyword_overrides are consulted at all -- unfixable from inside a dependent extension, only fixable by editing core's strong-anchor step itself.

As of this research, cslib/lean/typst manifest.json files in agent-system/extensions/ already carry only routing_agents + routing_agents_hard (no routing/routing_hard blocks) -- the routing-ladder-collapse-to-routing_agents-only work is further along than a task description referencing 'all four routing blocks' as current may assume. A new extension should check the live manifests directly rather than trust an older task description's routing-block count.

Established convention in this agent-system: every direct-execution (non-lifecycle) slash command pairs with a same-purpose skill directory invoked by that command, named skill-<domain>-<verb> (e.g. /vet <-> skill-cslib-vet, /pr <-> skill-pr-implementation), whose own SKILL.md description states 'Invoke for /<command> command.' This gives the command both a user-typed entry point and an agent-callable one. /lake and /lean are the exception: their logic is written inline in the command .md itself with a parallel skill-lake-repair/skill-lean-version directory of near-duplicate content, rather than the command delegating to the skill.

next_steps: Run /plan 297 to create the implementation plan for the books extension's manifest, agents, skills, commands, rule and tests, using this report's Decisions section as the fixed design (two routing blocks; books:certify only; --hard variants authored; /book and /certify as separate commands; flattened book-directory layout in the rule). Two follow-ups are recorded as added scope to spawn (not to absorb into 297 or its plan): (a) amend core's task-type-detect.sh strong-anchor step to close the .lean-filename-capture gap; (b) move the already-scoped 'Add reconcile command to agent system' work's deliverables from typst+lean into books.
